records.statement: exec runs a command inside the target container and streams its stdout/stderr and propagates its exit code, matching the reference.
records.notes: Backed by the declarative exec cases (case-exec-decl-tty, case-exec-decl-user, case-exec-decl-working-directory, case-exec-remote-env-propagation), which replaced the hand-written `parity_exec` carrier.

records.statement: exec --container-id (no --workspace-folder/--config) recovers remoteUser and remoteEnv from the container's devcontainer.metadata label — which up stamps at create time — and applies them, matching the reference. remoteEnv, which lives only in devcontainer.json, is thereby recoverable without the workspace.
records.notes: #322: up writes the merged devcontainer.metadata label (single-container, Dockerfile, and compose paths); exec/read-configuration/set-up read it back via the shared container_metadata::config_from_metadata_label helper. Evidence: case-exec-container-id-metadata — an INDEPENDENTLY reported case, which the earlier note recorded as deferred (T110) for want of a runtime-resolved container-id token in an operation's argv. `${CONTAINER_ID}` is that token: the runner substitutes the id observed after the case's `up`, and fails loud when an operation uses it before any container exists, so such a case cannot silently degrade into a workspace-addressed exec. It replaces `case-up-exec-parity` (parity_up_exec), which reported ONE outcome covering this behavior and bhv-up-exec-parity together.

records.statement: `exec` runs the command with the environment the user-env probe captured, with the PATH entries the image contributed via `ENV PATH` restored when the probe's login shell dropped them.
records.notes: Fixed under #370. Measured at oracle 0.87.0 against fx-exec-dockerfile-overlay: the image's `Config.Env` PATH is `/opt/conformance/bin:/usr/local/sbin:…`, and deacon's `exec` now reports exactly that, byte-identical to the reference; `conf-tool` resolves on both sides. The defect was a three-step composition — the probe runs a LOGIN shell whose `/etc/profile` ASSIGNS PATH (alpine:3.19 does), `build_effective_env` rebuilt the environment from that probe alone, and `build_exec_args` then re-asserted the degraded value as an explicit `-e PATH=`. `resolve_env_and_user` now restores the container's own PATH entries into the probe result before any of that, via `ContainerEnvironmentProber::merge_container_path`. ROOT CAUSE CORRECTION: the issue originally described this as an env-PRECEDENCE problem needing a per-variable policy for PATH. It is not. The reference does not resolve it by precedence at all — it REWRITES the container's `/etc/profile` to `export PATH=${PATH:-…}` so a login shell stops clobbering, and applies an in-process merge only when it may not change system config. deacon does not modify container system files, so it always takes the merge path. The residual that leaves — the relative order of a restored image entry against a Feature's `/etc/profile.d` entry — is recorded separately as `bhv-exec-restored-path-ordering`. `wvr-exec-image-path-dropped` was deleted with the fix.

records.statement: The relative order of a restored image `PATH` entry against one a Feature contributed through `/etc/profile.d`, when the probe's login shell dropped the image's.
records.notes: The residual left by the #370 fix, and a deliberate consequence of how deacon fixes it. Measured at oracle 0.87.0 over fx-exec-feature-path-ordering (the image contributes `/opt/image/bin` via `ENV PATH=`, a Feature contributes `/opt/feature/bin` via `/etc/profile.d`): the reference's `exec` reports `/opt/feature/bin:/opt/image/bin:...` and deacon's reports `/opt/image/bin:/opt/feature/bin:...`. BOTH entries are present on both sides and both tools resolve - only the relative order of two SURVIVING entries differs, so nothing is unreachable either way. The cause is that the two CLIs fix the same problem by different means. The reference REWRITES the container's `/etc/profile` to `export PATH=${PATH:-...}` so a login shell stops clobbering; its probe therefore never loses the image's entry, and the Feature's script prepends in front of a PATH that already has it. deacon does not modify the container's system files, so it RECONSTRUCTS instead - and reconstruction cannot recover an ordering the probe never reported. `intentional-divergence` is accurate rather than a placeholder: writing to a container's `/etc/profile` is a posture decision, not a bug fix, and it was weighed against this residual and declined. The spec says nothing about PATH ordering between contributors, hence `spec: unspecified`. Covered by `case-exec-feature-path-ordering` and pinned in unit tests on `merge_container_path`.
